A resting stop is a market order once touched, so filling every stop at the stop price is the single most common way a backtest manufactures money it could never have earned. Signals compute from bars[0..t] and are ACTED ON AT THE NEXT OPEN, never at the close that produced them, which costs a night of gap risk exactly as live trading does. Cash earns 0pct, biasing filtered rows downward.
r4_taken_apart: R4 is three separable mechanisms and the cost is almost entirely in one of them. R2 entry with NO STOP AT ALL: 9.45pct CAGR, 20.8pct max DD. ADD THE 8pct HARD STOP: 9.30pct, 20.4pct -- COSTS 0.15pp, essentially free. ADD THE BREAKEVEN RAISE: 9.03pct -- costs 0.27pp more. ADD THE 8pct TRAIL, which is FULL R4: 6.83pct, 18.3pct -- COSTS 2.20pp MORE. The trail alone is roughly ten times more expensive than the hard stop and the breakeven raise combined.
the_trail_cost_is_monotonic: Holding the 8pct initial stop fixed and varying ONLY the trail width: 8pct -> 6.83pct, 12pct -> 7.10pct, 15pct -> 7.61pct, 20pct -> 8.44pct, 25pct -> 8.81pct. Tighter is worse, without exception. The same pattern holds on a rule-1-only entry: 9.80pct with breakeven, 7.97pct with the 8pct trail, 9.10pct with a 20pct trail. Two independent entry rules, same conclusion.
the_win_rate_trap: WORTH KEEPING SEPARATELY BECAUSE IT IS COUNTERINTUITIVE. The trail RAISES the win rate from 27.4pct to 44.3pct while LOWERING CAGR from 9.03pct to 6.83pct, and cuts average hold from 68 days to 38. It manufactures the FEELING of being right by cutting short the small number of winners that pay for everything else. Any future evaluation of TARS that scores win rate rather than return will therefore reward exactly the wrong rule. expectancy.py should be read with this in mind.
the_regime_table_changed_the_recommendat: A single 20-year number can hide a rule that worked in 2008 and has lost money ever since, so the comparison was split by period. THE TRAIL IS NOT UNIFORMLY BAD. In 2020-2022 -- covid plus the 2022 bear -- FULL R4 returned 11.41pct against 10.55pct for no stop AND cut max drawdown from 15.4pct to 10.1pct. It is crash insurance. Over 20 years the premium exceeded the payout, but the payout is real and arrives precisely when a small account can least afford to be without it.
the_genuinely_damning_period: 2015-2019. The trail returned 5.17pct against 8.47pct for stop-plus-breakeven, AND ITS DRAWDOWN WAS WORSE: 15.1pct against 10.7pct. Insurance that loses money AND deepens the loss is not insurance. MECHANISM, and it is a design defect rather than bad luck: the trail sells into a dip, and then R2 RULE 3 REFUSES TO RE-ENTER UNTIL PRICE IS BACK WITHIN 5pct OF THE 20-DAY HIGH -- so the book buys back HIGHER than it sold. THE EXIT RULE AND THE ENTRY RULE FIGHT EACH OTHER. Neither rule is wrong alone; the pair is wrong. This is the first defect found in TARS that lives in the interaction between two rules rather than inside either one, and it would have been invisible to any test that examined R2 and R4 separately.
proposal_not_amendment: NO RULE CHANGED AND NO LIVE STOP MOVED. Widening the trail LOOSENS a constraint on the agent, and by R6's own standard a loosening proposed by the party it constrains does not take effect on that party's authority -- the same reason the R2 rule-3 widening was left to Nolan. It also would mean moving real stops on real money on seven live positions. Recommendation put to Nolan: KEEP the 8pct hard stop and the breakeven raise, both of which are cheap and measured; WIDEN the trail from 8pct to about 20pct. Expected effect on the 20-year test is roughly +1.6pp CAGR at the cost of about 1.3pp of max drawdown.
what_is_still_untested: R2 rule 4 (earnings blackout) and rule 5 (sector cap) are not price rules and remain unmeasured by anything. Slippage beyond the gap-fill rule, commissions and partial fills are not modelled. Intraday stop-running below the daily low is invisible at daily resolution. R6's circuit breaker is now testable with this dataset and has not been tested yet. Their absence is a limit of the test, not evidence they are free.

thesis: R6'S -15pct HALT HAS NO RESUME CONDITION. Nothing anywhere in the ruleset says how the system comes back after the halt fires. Found by building a portfolio simulator and running R6 literally as written: the book halted on 2008-04-11 and NEVER TRADED AGAIN. 44 trades in twenty years, 1,320 to 1,657, a 1.15pct CAGR against SPY's 8.71pct. Once the resume condition was supplied the same ruleset made 543 trades and 4,672.
why_nobody_noticed: Because in the live account it is masked. Nolan deposits money most weeks, R6 rebases the high-water mark on deposits, and a rebase silently clears the halt condition. The rule has been load-bearing-broken the entire time and his deposits have been holding it up. The account has never been far enough underwater for anyone to discover that the rule has no way out.
the_fix_proposed: Write the resume condition down explicitly. Proposed: a halt pauses NEW ENTRIES only, never forces exits, for a stated cooling-off period, after which the high-water mark rebases to current equity and entries resume. Modelled as 10 trading days. THIS IS A LOOSENING and is therefore NOT implemented on TARS's own authority. Note the asymmetry that makes it urgent anyway: as written, the failure mode is not 'too risky', it is 'silently stops working forever', and a rule that can permanently disable the system without saying so is worse than either a tight rule or a loose one.
general_lesson: This is the fourth defect of the same family: a rule that was never executed end-to-end under conditions it was written for. R12's stale 85, R9's inoperative flat 50, R3's flat 340, and now R6's missing resume. EVERY ONE was found by running the rule rather than reading it. Reading a ruleset cannot find a missing case; only executing it can.

thesis: THE 340 DOLLAR FLAT CAP IN R3 STRANGLES THE ACCOUNT AS IT GROWS, AND THE COST IS NOW MEASURED RATHER THAN PREDICTED. Out-of-sample 2016-2026, NVDA excluded, same ruleset, varying only starting capital: at 1,320 the cap costs 1.66pp per year; at 5,000 it costs 5.18pp; at 10,000 it costs 10.68pp; at 25,000 it costs 12.50pp. The account does not outgrow the rule, the rule progressively shuts the account down.
this_was_predicted_in_writing: THE SAME MORNING. 2026-09-21-R3-AMENDMENT-PERCENTAGE-CAP recorded, under known_future_problem: 'Above ~1700 the 340 dollar cap binds alone and keeps shrinking as a percentage... The 340 figure will need raising again, deliberately and in writing, somewhere in the 3000-5000 range.' The engine found it independently, which is the entire point of writing predictions down before they can be checked. The prediction was directionally right and UNDERSTATED the magnitude.
a_mislabelling_i_corrected: The engine's comparison table originally carried a row called 'risk-parity sizing (2pct/trade)' which appeared to add 1.88pp. IT DOES NO RISK PARITY. At 2pct risk with an 8pct stop the formula asks for equity*0.02/0.08 = 25pct of equity, which is always above the 20pct per-position cap, so the risk term NEVER BINDS and the cap does all the work. Verified bit-identical to simply removing the flat dollar cap: both return 13.25pct and finish at 4,987 to the dollar. The label was wrong and the finding underneath it was real but differently caused. Corrected in the file rather than left standing.
recommendation: Replace the flat 340 with a pure percentage, or index it to account value so it cannot go stale again. NOT implemented: raising a cap LOOSENS a constraint on the agent, which by R6's own standard is not TARS's call. But note this one is unlike the trail: leaving it in place is not the safe option, it is a measured and compounding cost that gets worse every week Nolan deposits.

thesis: I PREDICTED WHOLE-SHARE QUANTIZATION WOULD BE THE EXPENSIVE RULE AND I WAS WRONG. engine.py's docstring said so in writing before the test ran: 'R12 is the one I suspect costs the most.' Allowing fractional shares moves CAGR from 6.57pct to 6.78pct. That is noise. The reasoning behind the guess was sound -- on 2026-09-21 ABBV really did sit at 25.2pct of the book and INTC at 11.4pct purely because of their share prices -- but lumpy weights average out over hundreds of trades in a way a single day's snapshot cannot show.
what_actually_costs: R4's trail (4.33pp at portfolio level) and R3's flat dollar cap (1.66pp at this account size, 10.68pp at 10,000). The general lesson, which is worth more than the specific number: A CONSTANT THAT STOPS SCALING IS RUINOUS AND LOOKS FINE. LUMPY WEIGHTS LOOK WRONG AND MOSTLY ARE NOT. TARS's intuition ranked the visible problem above the invisible one, which is the direction intuition always errs.
handling: The wrong guess was left visible in engine.py above the answer rather than quietly deleted, so the file records a prediction that failed instead of presenting only conclusions that worked.

thesis: THE 'SELL INTO A DIP, BUY BACK HIGHER' DEFECT IS REAL BUT ABOUT A THIRD THE SIZE THE RAW NUMBER SUGGESTS. Measured directly on consecutive round trips in the same name, 2016-2026: 74.5pct of re-entries were ABOVE the price the position was sold at, mean gap +3.49pct, n=290. That looks damning on its own.
the_null_that_nearly_killed_the_finding: STOCKS DRIFT UP, so a majority of re-entries would be higher even from random timing, and quoting 74.5pct without saying so would have been a dishonest number. Null computed on the same universe and window with RANDOM entry days: 56.4pct up at 10 days, 59.6pct at 40 days (the observed average wait), 61.8pct at 90 days; mean forward move +2.50pct at 40 days. So the honest finding is 74.5pct against a 59.6pct null and +3.49pct against a +2.50pct null -- the rule interaction costs roughly ONE POINT PER ROUND TRIP, not three and a half. Real, worth fixing, and not the headline it first appeared to be.
fix_not_identified: Loosening R2 rule 3 was tested as the candidate fix and DOES NOT RELIABLY HELP: out-of-sample and NVDA-free, rule 3 at 5pct gives 13.25pct, at 10pct 12.49pct, at 15pct 14.98pct, off entirely 13.55pct. That is not a mechanism, that is noise with a trend drawn through it. NO CHANGE RECOMMENDED to rule 3 on this evidence. Recorded so that a future session does not re-derive the idea and mistake the 15pct row for a finding.

thesis: A RESEARCH AGENT CLAIMED WHOLE-SHARE ROUNDING IS THE DOMINANT PROBLEM FOR THIS ACCOUNT, IDLING 8-27PCT OF CAPITAL, AND THAT FIXING IT IS 'WORTH MORE THAN ANY STRATEGY REFINEMENT'. TESTED AND REJECTED FOR THIS ACCOUNT. The claim is arithmetically correct for the sizing scheme it assumes and that is not the scheme TARS uses.
the_mechanism: The agent models 7 INDEPENDENT slots of 188.57, floors each one, and strands every remainder. At the account's real holding prices that strands 524.40, or 39.7pct -- even worse than the agent's own range, because ABBV at 264.69 and NVDA at 213.92 each exceed a 188.57 slot entirely and buy ZERO shares. TARS DEPLOYS SEQUENTIALLY: deployable is decremented by ACTUAL spend, so one position's rounding waste becomes the next position's budget. Same prices, same whole-share rule, sequential deployment leaves 5.68 idle, or 0.4pct. Rounding waste is RECYCLED, not stranded.
confirmed_by_the_engine: Independently and from the other direction: engine.py measures fractional shares at 12.47pct CAGR against 13.25pct for whole shares out-of-sample -- fractional was WORSE, though the gap is within noise. Two independent methods agree the granularity cost is near zero here. The agent's headline recommendation is not actionable and was not actioned.
what_survives_and_it_matters: TWO PARTS OF THE AGENT'S SECTION 4 ARE CORRECT AND USEFUL. (1) A HARD CEILING: any instrument priced above the per-position cap cannot be bought at all. SPY at 773.53, QQQ at 741.45 and IWM at 285.57 are all uninvestable in this account today, and ABBV at 264.69 already exceeds the 263 cap -- which is why it is grandfathered. (2) THE PENNY-TICK SPREAD FLOOR under Reg NMS Rule 612: one cent is a minimum spread, so percentage spread is bounded below by 1/price. A 2 dollar stock cannot trade tighter than 50bp, an 8 dollar stock than 12.5bp, a 20 dollar stock than 5bp. The agent also verified the half-penny amendment is delayed to November 2027, so this binds for the whole horizon.
this_contradicts_something_i_did_today: THE R3 GRANULARITY AMENDMENT MADE THIS MORNING PUSHES TOWARD CHEAP STOCKS AND THE TICK FLOOR SAYS CHEAP STOCKS COST MORE TO TRADE. The amendment set a 3-share preference, which on a 65 dollar deployable meant screening at or below 21.72 -- and the pre-registered plan's alternates included ITUB at 8.375, where one cent is 12bp of minimum spread against roughly 5bp for NWG at 18.98. The granularity preference was written without pricing the spread it buys. NOT a reversal of the amendment, which is still sound, but it needs a FLOOR as well as a ceiling. Proposed: prefer candidates above roughly 15 dollars per share, where the tick floor is under 7bp. Recorded as a proposal.
process_note: Prices in the agent's report were spot-checked against the broker before any of it was used: SPY 773.53, QQQ 741.45, IWM 285.57, RSP 212.70, SCHB 29.84, SCHG 36.26 all matched to the cent. The agent also self-reported that a fetched FRED yield series looked fabricated by a page summarizer and that it had corrected a stale breadth claim. Agent output is evidence to be checked, never authority.

thesis: THE RESEARCH AGENT'S SINGLE HIGHEST-VALUE SUGGESTION WAS TESTED AND REJECTED. Its reasoning was sound and its facts checked out: a 200-day system was whipsawed three times in 2026, SPY and QQQ both sold 2026-03-20 and rebought 2026-04-08 about 4.3pct higher, and IWM generated a ONE-DAY signal on 2026-03-30 costing 3.5pct. It proposed requiring confirmation -- N consecutive closes, or a band below the MA -- before an exit counts.
it_looked_excellent_on_the_first_test: Out-of-sample 2016-2026, NVDA-free: no band 13.25pct, 1pct band 15.51pct, 3pct band 14.95pct, 5pct band 14.94pct. EVERY band value beat no band, Sharpe 0.94 to 1.05. That is a proper parameter neighbourhood rather than one lucky value, and on that evidence it was the best-supported change of the night.
the_walk_forward_killed_it: THE 1PCT BAND BEAT NO BAND IN ONLY 3 OF 9 ROLLING TWO-YEAR WINDOWS. Worse, it REVERSED across the split: in-sample 2006-2015 it HURT, 13.02pct down to 12.51pct at 1pct and 10.22pct at 3pct, while out-of-sample it helped. A change that loses in the decade you would have chosen it in and wins in the decade you report is the weakest evidential shape there is -- it could never have been selected honestly, so the out-of-sample gain is luck rather than mechanism. Driven by two windows, 2021-2022 at +7.35pp and 2015-2016 at +2.01pp, losing in six of nine.
the_general_lesson: 'THIS WOULD HAVE HELPED IN 2026' IS NOT 'THIS HELPS ON AVERAGE'. The agent reasoned from a real and correctly documented feature of the current year. A rule chosen to fix the most recent thing that hurt is fitted to the most recent thing that hurt. This is the SECOND finding of the session killed by the rolling walk-forward, after the TARS-2 headline, and both times the single split-sample test had passed it. One split can be lucky; nine windows are harder to fool. The walk-forward is now the standard any proposed rule change must clear.
no_change_made: Exit confirmation is implemented in engine.py as exit_confirm and exit_band so the finding is reproducible, but both default to OFF and no rule was amended.

thesis: TARS-2 IS NOW FULLY SPECIFIED IN TARS_RULES.md AND IS EXPLICITLY NOT ACTIVE. The live account still trades TARS-1. Switching would move every stop on seven live positions, which is a real-money act and Nolan's to authorise; the specification exists so that decision is made against written evidence rather than against TARS's say-so. Four proposed changes: R2' collapses entry and exit onto ONE threshold (delete the 50-day MA and the within-5pct-of-20-day-high gate); R4' keeps the 8pct hard stop and the breakeven raise and DELETES the trail; R3' replaces the 340 dollar flat cap with a pure 20pct; R6' gives the halt a written resume condition.
the_headline_change: R2' IS THE ONE WITH FOUR INDEPENDENT LINES OF SUPPORT. The defect is INVERTED HYSTERESIS: TARS-1's exit is easier to trip than its re-entry, so every round trip is structurally biased to sell low and buy higher. (1) MEASURED FIRST, before any reading: 74.5pct of same-name re-entries were above the exit price against a 59.6pct drift null, costing about one point per round trip. (2) PUBLISHED: Clare/Seaton/Smith/Thomas show performance rising MONOTONICALLY as the exit window approaches the entry window, 2.48pct at Sharpe -0.19 for maximum asymmetry up to 11.19pct at 0.59 fully symmetric. (3) MECHANISM: Byun and Jeon 2023 find 52-week losers beat winners by over 3.36pct/month during rebounds, so a nearness-to-high re-entry gate excludes the best population exactly in the recovery -- which predicts BOTH observed symptoms, the lost return and the worse drawdown. (4) WALK-FORWARD: beat TARS-1 in 7 of 9 windows, improved in BOTH halves of the split with no reversal, survived dropping NVDA at +3.94pp and dropping the four largest winners at +1.54pp, smooth lookback neighbourhood across 150-400 days, turnover down to 1.79 round-trips per name per year.
the_trail_finding_replicates_on_90_years: R4's 8pct trail measured at -2.20pp per year on 14 names. Dai 2021 tests trailing stops from 1pct to 20pct on 25,997 US STOCKS OVER 1926-2016 and reports value-weighted monthly returns of 0.43/0.45/0.63/0.79pct at 1/5/10/20pct against a 0.76pct benchmark -- MONOTONE, with only the 20pct stop beating doing nothing. Clare et al find every stop width loses to no stop and conclude 'a change of trend is the best stop loss'. UNCOMFORTABLE COINCIDENCE RECORDED: Lei and Li note average daily sigma of 1.65pct, making a 5-standard-deviation stop 8.25pct -- so TARS-1's 8pct is almost exactly the TIGHTEST SETTING ANYONE IN THE LITERATURE TESTS, picked from intuition and landing on the worst-supported number in the field. Kaminski and Lo supply the mechanism: a stop adds expected return only when autocorrelation exceeds the Sharpe ratio at the same sampling frequency, and a tight trail samples where daily autocorrelation is near zero.
two_proposals_killed_at_the_walk_forward: RECORDED SO THEY ARE NOT RE-DERIVED. (1) EXIT CONFIRMATION BAND, which was the research agent's top suggestion and the best-supported idea of the night on the first test -- every band from 1pct to 5pct beat no band, Sharpe 0.94 to 1.05. The walk-forward killed it: 3 of 9 windows, and it REVERSED across the split, losing in the decade it would have been chosen in. (2) ATR-MULTIPLE STOPS, which scored 7.68pct against 6.57pct but are indistinguishable from simply having a wider stop, and for which the research found NO peer-reviewed test on long-only US equities at all. General lesson written into the file: 'this would have helped in 2026' is not 'this helps on average'.
what_tempers_all_of_it: ACROSS NINE ROLLING WINDOWS THE BEST CANDIDATE BEAT SPY IN ONLY 5 OF 9. The aggregate edge is real; its RELIABILITY is not. Faber's own model underperforms the index in roughly half of all years since 1901 and the SG Trend Index returned 0.4pct annualised over 2009-2019. Any version of this will spend whole years looking broken, and that has to be budgeted for BEFORE switching rather than discovered after. Survivorship is also real and unfixed: all 14 names survived to 2026, so every absolute CAGR in the section is flattered and only the between-ruleset comparisons transfer.

thesis: NOLAN DIRECTED THE DEFECT FIXES ('Fix the R6 halt bug and fix the other bugs I need you to work not have all these bugs'). THREE ADOPTED AND NOW LIVE, ONE DELIBERATELY EXCLUDED. (1) R6's -15pct halt now has a written RESUME CONDITION: it pauses new entries only, never forces an exit, and after 10 completed trading days the high-water mark rebases to current account value and entries resume, with Nolan told when it fires and when it clears. As written before today it was a ONE-WAY LATCH with no way back -- run literally in simulation the book halted 2008-04-11 and never traded again, 44 trades in eighteen years. (2) R3's 340 dollar flat cap DELETED; the per-position cap is now a pure 20pct of account value. (3) R2's rules 2 and 3 (the 50-day MA and the within-5pct-of-20-day-high gate) DELETED, and R4's trend exit changed to the 200-day alone, so ONE threshold is used in both directions.
what_was_excluded_and_why: R4's 8pct TRAIL IS NOT TOUCHED AND REMAINS IN FORCE. It costs roughly 2.2pp per year and that is measured, but it is a CRASH-INSURANCE TRADEOFF, NOT A BUG -- in 2020-2022 it beat no-stop on return AND cut drawdown from 15.4pct to 10.1pct. Nolan asked for bugs to be fixed; deleting the trail is a separate decision he has not made, and sweeping it in under 'fix the bugs' would have been taking a judgement call on his behalf. Also noted: deleting the trail would raise the question of what happens to INTC's stop, which is currently TRAILED ABOVE ENTRY at 112.04 locking +10.2pct, and R4's never-lower rule would keep it there regardless.
no_live_stop_moved: CONFIRMED. All three adopted changes touch sizing, signals and the halt. NONE of them touches a placed GTC stop order. The per-position cap is unchanged in practice today: 20pct of 1,321.13 is 264.23, and the superseded min(340, 20pct) also evaluated to 264.23 at this account size, so the percentage was already binding and the deletion changes nothing until the account passes about 1,700.
an_error_i_made_and_caught: THE FIRST DRAFT OF THE R2 WRITE-UP CLAIMED EXITS WOULD BECOME LATER. THAT WAS WRONG AND IT WAS CAUGHT BY RUNNING THE ENGINE RATHER THAN BY RE-READING THE SENTENCE. 'Below the 200-day' is a SUPERSET of 'below both MAs' -- in a decline price loses the 50-day first, so the two rules agree in most downtrends, but in a RECOVERY price can reclaim the 50-day while still under the 200-day, and the old rule then stopped exiting while the new one still does. Measured with entry held fixed, 2016-2026: trend exits rise 150 to 191 and average hold FALLS from 62 to 54 days, CAGR 13.55 to 13.85pct. The wrong version is named in the rules file rather than quietly replaced, because it is the same lesson as the R6 bug sitting directly above it: reasoning about a rule is not executing it.

thesis: SOFI FAILS R4'S TREND EXIT AND IS OVERDUE, UNDER BOTH THE OLD RULE AND THE NEW ONE. Measured on the completed 2026-09-21 daily bar as both rules require: close 16.97, 50-day SMA 17.6797, 200-day SMA 19.4530. THE CLOSE IS BELOW BOTH -- 4.0pct below the 50-day and 12.8pct below the 200-day. the_numbers_for_the_decision: 10 shares at 17.15 live is about 171.50, roughly 13pct of the book. thesis: NOLAN OVERRODE THE SOFI EXIT AND THE OVERRIDE IS HIS TO MAKE. In his words: 'Honestly no that's gonna be over a 20 dollar stock in a year or 2 I want to hold them act as almost you don't see it.' TARS had surfaced that SOFI fails R4's trend exit on the 2026-09-21 close under BOTH the old and the new rule -- close 16.97 against a 50-day SMA of 17.6797 and a 200-day SMA of 19.4530, below both -- and that R11 had required an exit at takeover which was never executed. Nolan has a 1-2 year thesis and a price target above 20. That is a discretionary hold on his own position, not a mechanical decision, and it is logged as his.
what_ignore_it_actually_means: SOFI IS NOW CARVED OUT OF THE MECHANICAL SYSTEM, and the carve-out has to be specific or it becomes a loophole. (1) R4's trend exit NO LONGER APPLIES to SOFI. TARS will not raise the exit again and will not re-litigate it at every check. It was never a TARS-1 entry, never passed R2 rule 1, and crediting or blaming the system for it would corrupt the track record. 'Act like you don't see it' cannot extend to pretending the capital is not there.
the_stop_is_the_open_question_and_was_ra: SOFI'S STOP REMAINS AT 15.75 AND TARS FLAGGED THE CONTRADICTION RATHER THAN LEAVING IT BURIED: an 8pct stop and a 1-2 year hold are incompatible, because an ordinary dip sells the position out from under the thesis. Nolan has not yet said which he wants. LEAVING THE STOP IS THE DEFAULT because removing protection on an unstated assumption is the worse error of the two, and a stop can be cancelled in seconds if he says so. To be revisited at his word, not on TARS's initiative.
scoring_note: Recorded so a future session does not rediscover the failed trend test and re-raise it as new. The exit signal is real, it is known, and it was overridden deliberately by the account owner.

CANDIDATE: CVE, Cenovus Energy, an integrated Canadian oil company, roughly 31.41 at the time of writing. CANNOT BE BOUGHT TODAY and the reason is CASH, not the circuit breaker: cash 224.54 real against a 15pct floor of 198.38 on a 1,322.55 account leaves 26.16 DEPLOYABLE, and one share costs 31.41.
